For any single fifth-degree polynomial \(f(x)\), if the recorded values are the arithmetic progression \(y_i = y_1+(i-1)d\), then for indices \(i\) where \(f\) is used,

\[
f(a+i-1)-\bigl(y_1+(i-1)d\bigr)=0.
\]

The left side is a polynomial in \(i\) of degree \(5\), so it has at most \(5\) roots. Thus one polynomial can be used for at most \(5\) called numbers. With \(10\) polynomials, the total is at most

\[
10\cdot 5=50.
\]

This bound is achievable: take the called numbers \(1,2,\dots,50\), and let the arithmetic progression be \(1,2,\dots,50\). For each block of five consecutive numbers \(5j+1,\dots,5j+5\), use

\[
P_j(x)=x+\prod_{r=1}^5 \bigl(x-(5j+r)\bigr),
\]

which is fifth-degree and equals \(x\) on that block. Then the written values form the arithmetic progression \(1,2,\dots,50\).

\[
\boxed{50}
\]
